The response is correct. The stored values of 0.1 and 0.2 in IEEE 754 double precision are accurately quoted (about 0.1000000000000000055511 and 0.2000000000000000111022), and their sum rounds to the double nearest 0.30000000000000004, which differs from the double nearest 0.3. It identifies the key cause: binary floating-point cannot represent these decimal fractions exactly, so rounding error appears. The 1/3 analogy helps, and the practical advice (tolerance comparisons or decimal types) is useful. It stays under 120 words. The one small gap is that it doesn't say explicitly that the error is a property of base-2 representation, though the text implies it.
